network.tdh.spec.metadataDescription: The exact rule behind TDH: every input, formula and rounding step, in readable form.
network.tdh.spec.title: The TDH-v1 specification
network.tdh.spec.lede: TDH-v1 is the exact rule behind TDH, written so that independent programs produce identical results, to the last unit. It restates the formula 6529.io has always used. Where it departs from the old backend, it removes a dependence on timing, database order, editable data or floating-point evaluation, and section 11 lists each departure with its measured effect.
network.tdh.spec.version: Rule version tdh-v1.0. Specification P26, text of 15 October 2026. It is the rule 6529.io and every validator compute; its adoption as the consensus rule of the future chain remains the owner’s decision.
network.tdh.spec.pendingD131: Decided on 15 October 2026 and not yet in the text below: movements within one transaction are netted (section 7, D131).
network.tdh.spec.mapDesc: Inputs (section 2) feed canonical events (3), which set the snapshot (4). Eligibility and rates (5) and identities (6) feed holdings (7), which feed scores (8) and the day’s output (9). Parameters (10) feed sections 5 to 8.
network.tdh.spec.s1.title: 1. Scope and conventions
network.tdh.spec.s1.body: TDH-v1 defines, for one day, each wallet’s and each identity’s balance, whole days, base, boost and final TDH for every eligible token, and the network totals. Ranks, xTDH, REP and upload files are out of scope. All arithmetic is on integers or exact fractions. Where the old backend’s floating-point rounding matters, the rule names it exactly: B64 is the nearest binary64 number, and it only decides ties.
network.tdh.spec.s2.title: 2. Inputs
network.tdh.spec.s2.body: One day’s inputs are Ethereum’s canonical chain up to the snapshot block, every event of five contracts up to that block, and the rule version’s parameter list. Prices, Meme Lab, received xTDH, REP and $6529 balances are not inputs.
network.tdh.spec.s2.delegationEvents: Register and revoke, direct and through a sub-delegate
network.tdh.spec.s2.manifoldEvents: getClaimForToken, read at the snapshot block
network.tdh.spec.s2.topicsCaption: Topic hashes, keccak-256 of each signature
network.tdh.spec.s3.title: 3. Canonical events
network.tdh.spec.s3.body: Every event is read exactly once, decoded strictly, and put in one order that everyone can reproduce: block, then transaction, then log, then position in a batch. A node that cannot show it has every event must not publish. A malformed event invalidates the day’s input rather than being skipped. Zero-amount and self transfers move nothing but are kept, because a zero-amount mint is how a card is created.
network.tdh.spec.s3.sinks: Mints, burns and sinks: a mint comes from the zero address and debits nobody. A transfer to the zero address or 0x…dEaD is a burn; the sinks receive records but are never debited. The FirstGM burn transaction is not credited to the zero address. Burns do not reduce edition sizes.
network.tdh.spec.s3.d131: Decided by D131, text pending: within one transaction, each wallet’s movements of each token are netted and applied at the transaction’s position.
network.tdh.spec.s4.title: 4. Day, snapshot and whole days
network.tdh.spec.s4.body: Day N is the number of days since 1 January 1970; it closes at N × 86,400 seconds, 00:00 UTC. The snapshot block is the last block before that moment on the finalized chain, and the day has no result until the next block is finalized too. Ages are whole days measured to the snapshot block’s time. Example: the upload dated 2026-10-11 is day 20,737, boundary 1,791,676,800.
network.tdh.spec.s4.binds: The result binds (N, B, hash(B), T, rule version, registry hash).
network.tdh.spec.s5.title: 5. Eligibility, editions, rates and seasons
network.tdh.spec.s5-1.title: 5.1 Eligibility
network.tdh.spec.s5-1.body: Memes and Gradients count when their first mint, of any amount, is at least eligibility_min_age_s (86,400 s) before T. NextGen tokens count when minted at or before B. n_memes is the number of eligible Memes, a count.
network.tdh.spec.s5-2.title: 5.2 Editions and floors
network.tdh.spec.s5-2.body: Burns do not reduce an edition. FirstGM’s edition is adjusted by −2,588. A Meme with fewer than 300 copies gets a floor, its claim’s totalMax capped at 310, and its edition is the larger of the floor and the minted count, because the final top-up airdrop takes it to 310, above the Nakamoto Threshold of 300. From 300 copies on there is no floor. A Meme with no claim has no floor. A Meme with an effective edition of 0 is eligible but has no rate, and holding a copy of it makes the input invalid.
network.tdh.spec.s5-3.title: 5.3 Rates
network.tdh.spec.s5-3.body: Meme i: RATE(H, E[i]). Gradient: RATE(H, G), at least 1.00, G = Gradients minted at or before B. NextGen token t: RATE(H, N_c), c = t div 10^10, N_c = tokens of collection c minted at or before B. With no eligible Meme, H = 0: Gradients get 1.00 and NextGen 0.
network.tdh.spec.s5-4.title: 5.4 Seasons
network.tdh.spec.s5-4.body: Seasons come from a versioned list of first Meme ids: 1, 48, 87, 119, 152, 181, 213, 246, 279, 311, 343, 375, 407, 439, 477, 516, 556. A season is listed for a day when its first id is at most n_memes; the highest listed is current. Seasons 1 to 20 carry a 0.05 bonus; a season pays when it is not current and its bonus is positive. A new season must be added, as a new rule version, before its first card becomes eligible.
network.tdh.spec.s6.title: 6. Consolidation
network.tdh.spec.s6-1.title: 6.1 Events
network.tdh.spec.s6-1.body: Only delegation events with use case 999, for The Memes or the all-collections address 0x8888…8888, between two different wallets, count. Expiry, allTokens, token id and update events are ignored.
network.tdh.spec.s6-2.title: 6.2 Pair state
network.tdh.spec.s6-2.body: Each unordered pair of wallets has at most one row. A registration in one direction is pending; the other direction confirms it. The collection does not partition the state.
network.tdh.spec.s6-2.machineDesc: Three states: no row, pending from a to b, and confirmed. REGISTER(a, b) creates a pending row; REGISTER(b, a) on a pending row confirms it. REVOKE on a confirmed row returns it to pending in the other direction; REVOKE by the registering side of a pending row deletes it.
network.tdh.spec.s6-3.title: 6.3 Identities
network.tdh.spec.s6-3.body: Confirmed pairs, newest first, grow cliques of at most 3 wallets in which every pair is confirmed; a wallet joins at most one.
network.tdh.spec.s6-4.title: 6.4 and 6.5 Effective state and identity key
network.tdh.spec.s6-4.body: The grouping after all events up to B applies to the whole history of the day’s calculation. An identity’s key is its sorted lowercase addresses joined by “-”.
network.tdh.spec.s7.title: 7. Holdings
network.tdh.spec.s7.body: Replay every transfer in canonical order, keeping a list of acquisition times per wallet and token; sends take from the end; age carries only between wallets of one identity. Base per token is rounded per wallet; an identity’s base is the sum of its wallets’ bases, never recomputed from merged days. A wallet has a record when it holds an eligible token or belongs to a group; an identity has a record when one of its wallets does.
network.tdh.spec.s7.d131: Decided by D131, text pending: the replay applies each transaction’s net change per wallet and token.
network.tdh.spec.s8.title: 8. Arithmetic and scores
network.tdh.spec.s8-1.title: 8.1 Rate
network.tdh.spec.s8-1.body: RATE equals half-up of 100n/d except at an exact half cent; with H = 3,941 that happens only for editions 8, 40, 56, 200, 280 and 1,400.
network.tdh.spec.s8-2.title: 8.2 Base
network.tdh.spec.s8-2.body: BASE equals the old two-step rounding.
network.tdh.spec.s8-3.title: 8.3 Boost
network.tdh.spec.s8-3.body: A record holds a token when the token is eligible and the balance is positive, whatever the copies’ ages. ADD(2) = 50,000, ADD(3) = 82,645, ADD(n) = 144,051 for n ≥ 33; the cent rounding never meets a tie.
network.tdh.spec.s8-4.title: 8.4 Final
network.tdh.spec.s8-4.body: FINAL is computed per token; a record’s final is the sum. Ties round down only for some boosts and some bases, the smallest being base 25 at 1.14.
network.tdh.spec.s8-5.title: 8.5 Totals
network.tdh.spec.s8-5.body: The total is the sum of identity finals; a second total excludes the zero and dead identities, which never enter any consensus weight.
network.tdh.spec.s8-6.title: 8.6 Daily rate
network.tdh.spec.s8-6.body: rate_e4 = beta × the sum of the rates of each copy with at least one whole day, in 10^-4 TDH a day; derived data.
network.tdh.spec.s8-7.title: 8.7 Range
network.tdh.spec.s8-7.body: A day is inside the tdh-v1.0 range when H, G, every N_c, every base × beta and the total are below 2^53; outside it there is no result. Inside it, hardware binary64 and exact emulation agree.
network.tdh.spec.s9.title: 9. The day’s output
network.tdh.spec.s9.body: The header (N, B, hash(B), T, rule version, registry hash), and per identity its key, wallets, boost and final, with per-token balance, raw, base and final. The per-token final is what card-set credit uses. Wallet records, daily rates and totals are derived.
network.tdh.spec.s10.title: 10. Parameters
network.tdh.spec.s10.body: Every number the rule uses is a parameter of the rule version. Changing any of them makes a new rule version with its own start day.
network.tdh.spec.s10.name: Name
network.tdh.spec.s10.hashNote: Recomputed with the Python reference; conformance vector 28 checks it.
network.tdh.spec.param.nextgen_collectio: A NextGen collection id is the token id divided by this
network.tdh.spec.param.eligibility_min_a: A card counts after one full day
network.tdh.spec.param.day_s: Length of a whole holding day
network.tdh.spec.param.age_reference: Ages are measured to the snapshot block’s time
network.tdh.spec.param.cutoff_finality: The snapshot comes from the finalized chain
network.tdh.spec.param.firstgm_burn_tx: The adjustment’s burn is not also credited to the zero address
network.tdh.spec.param.edition_floor_cap: The top-up target: a floor is the claim limit, at most this
network.tdh.spec.param.edition_floor_thr: Floors apply only below this many copies
network.tdh.spec.param.gradient_rate_min: A Gradient’s rate never falls below this
network.tdh.spec.param.consolidation_use: The delegation use case for consolidation
network.tdh.spec.param.consolidation_col: Collection values a consolidation may name
network.tdh.spec.param.boost_decimals: The boost is rounded to cents
network.tdh.spec.param.boost_intermediat: ADD and the Meme bonus are rounded to micro-units
network.tdh.spec.param.season: Bonus per complete season, for seasons up to 20
network.tdh.spec.param.additional_set: First extra-set bonus and its geometric ratio
network.tdh.spec.param.gradient: Bonus per Gradient, and how many count
network.tdh.spec.param.season_starts: The first Meme id of each season
network.tdh.spec.s11.title: 11. Where TDH-v1 differs from the old backend
network.tdh.spec.s11.body: Nineteen differences, each listed with what the old backend did, what TDH-v1 does, the measured effect and the decision. Only one changed any value on the replayed cycle: DEV-2.
network.tdh.spec.s11.tableCaption: Deviations from the old backend, {shown} of 19 shown
network.tdh.spec.dev.1.old: Transfers came from an indexing service, merged per transaction
network.tdh.spec.dev.1.v1: One transfer per event, in on-chain order
network.tdh.spec.dev.2.old: Same-second movements ordered by a rule that depends on the wallet and on database order
network.tdh.spec.dev.2.v1: On-chain order; within one transaction, netting (D131)
network.tdh.spec.dev.2.effect: 2 identities, −241 TDH: a token sent out and back in one transaction
network.tdh.spec.dev.3.old: Snapshot block found at 00:01 on the unfinalized chain
network.tdh.spec.dev.4.old: Read whatever had been indexed by 00:01
network.tdh.spec.dev.4.v1: A complete, finalized set of events
network.tdh.spec.dev.4.effect: None that day; one late transfer in a year
network.tdh.spec.dev.5.v1: The first mint of any amount starts the clock
network.tdh.spec.dev.6.old: Edition floors kept in a database, refreshed for recent Memes only
network.tdh.spec.dev.6.v1: Read at the snapshot block, below 300 copies only
network.tdh.spec.dev.7.old: Gradient and NextGen rates from current database totals
network.tdh.spec.dev.7.v1: From on-chain counts at the snapshot block
network.tdh.spec.dev.8.v1: A versioned list of season starts
network.tdh.spec.dev.9.old: Consolidations read when the job runs, recomputed during the day
network.tdh.spec.dev.10.old: Today’s grouping applied to the whole history
network.tdh.spec.dev.11.old: Ties between links broken by database order
network.tdh.spec.dev.12.old: Link state ignores collection, expiry and updates
network.tdh.spec.dev.13.old: Zero and dead addresses get records and enter totals
network.tdh.spec.dev.13.v1: Records kept; never in consensus weight
network.tdh.spec.dev.15.old: Rates and boosts with floating point
network.tdh.spec.dev.16.old: A send larger than the holding silently removed fewer copies
network.tdh.spec.dev.17.old: Ages measured to the snapshot block’s time
network.tdh.spec.dev.18.old: Undefined results with no eligible Meme
network.tdh.spec.dev.19.old: A Meme with no copies got an infinite rate
network.tdh.spec.dev.19.v1: Eligible, no rate; holding it invalidates the input
network.tdh.spec.decision.adopted: Adopted; no value changed on the replayed cycle (D121)
network.tdh.spec.decision.dev2: TDH-v1’s order (D121); within a transaction, netting (D131)
network.tdh.spec.decision.dev13: Sink records kept, excluded from consensus weight (D121)
network.tdh.spec.s12.title: 12. Issues found in the old backend
network.tdh.spec.s12.body: Fifteen issues the work on TDH-v1 found in the old backend’s calculation, each with the TDH-v1 rule that removes it.
network.tdh.spec.bug.1.issue: The same-second ordering rule is inconsistent and can crash the run
network.tdh.spec.bug.2.issue: The order before sorting depends on which database query finishes first
network.tdh.spec.bug.3.issue: Indexing merges movements and drops their position
network.tdh.spec.bug.4.issue: Indexing follows the unfinalized chain and never revisits blocks
network.tdh.spec.bug.5.issue: The job does not wait for indexing to catch up
network.tdh.spec.bug.6.issue: The snapshot block search uses the unfinalized head
network.tdh.spec.bug.7.issue: Grouping changes rewrite history, and a day’s values can change after publication
network.tdh.spec.bug.7.fixed: Grouping as of the snapshot block (DEV-9)
network.tdh.spec.bug.8.issue: Link ties are ordered differently in two code paths
network.tdh.spec.bug.9.issue: Revoking one registration can unlink a pair confirmed under another collection
network.tdh.spec.bug.10.issue: Floors read at the latest state, failures dropped silently
network.tdh.spec.bug.10.fixed: Floors read at the snapshot block (DEV-6)
network.tdh.spec.bug.11.issue: Gradient and NextGen rates from current totals
network.tdh.spec.bug.12.issue: Seasons from editable metadata; a missing trait creates a phantom season
network.tdh.spec.bug.13.issue: Two different definitions of a mint
network.tdh.spec.bug.14.issue: An oversized send removes fewer copies than requested
network.tdh.spec.bug.15.issue: Uploads mix in current values for some columns
network.tdh.spec.s13.title: 13. Conformance
network.tdh.spec.s13.body: A program conforms when it reproduces every one of the 36 conformance vectors and, for a real day, the reference implementation’s output from the same inputs. The Python reference, the Rust core and program B pass all 36.
network.tdh.spec.decisions.title: Decisions referenced
network.tdh.spec.decisions.intro: The owner’s decisions these pages cite. The decision record is published with the validator code.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D112: Validator v1 agrees on TDH once a day, peer to peer: each validator computes TDH-v1 with the Rust core, signs the result and compares it with 6529.io.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D116: The validator code is licensed under Apache 2.0 and is published, with the TDH-v1 core and the conformance vectors, before the first outside operator runs it.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D118: Every validator checks each block’s events against Ethereum’s block headers, and the headers against a finalized block its own light client follows; a node that cannot complete the checks does not sign.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D119: Two separately written programs, A and B, prove each day’s result from Ethereum’s own history in two different zero-knowledge virtual machines.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D121: One TDH formula everywhere: 6529.io, its backend and the validators compute identical TDH with the validators’ Rust core; the open deviations are settled as listed in section 11.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D125: Every validator computes TDH with two separately written implementations before it signs, and does not sign if they disagree; anyone can add the Python reference as a third.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D128: A minimal Ethereum contract records a day’s result once both programs’ proofs verify; built and tested, deployed only when the owner approves.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D130: A new validator may take the TDH history from the network’s agreement, or check all of it itself.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D131: Ownership is read at transaction boundaries: each wallet’s movements of each token within one transaction are netted.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D132: From 16 October 2026 the Rust core and the Python reference run daily beside 6529.io’s backend and are shown side by side; 6529.io switches to the Rust result about one week later, around 23 October 2026.
network.tdh.spec.evidence.title: Evidence
network.tdh.spec.evidence.replay.title: Replay of 2026-10-11
network.tdh.spec.evidence.replay.body: From the live per-token inputs, TDH-v1 reproduces all 132,481 wallet-token bases and every wallet and identity value. From the 388,335 indexed transfers it reproduces 10,278 of 10,280 identities and 11,128 of 11,130 wallets; the two others are a token sent out and back in one transaction (DEV-2, −241 TDH in total). The cycle’s raw logs equal the indexed rows (69 of 69). A full replay from raw logs since 2021 was not run.
network.tdh.spec.evidence.cleanRoom.body: A second Rust implementation written from the specification alone found 23 places where it had to guess (2 high, 11 medium, 10 low). Each now has a rule in P26 and vectors that pin it.
network.tdh.spec.evidence.comparison.bod: From independent inputs (Ethereum logs, history not yet fully checked), the Rust core reproduced, each day, 10,280 of 10,282 identities and 11,131 of 11,133 wallets of 6529.io’s published files in every field. The two others were tokens sent out and back within one transaction, class A (DEV-2), which D131’s netting settles.
